content_sections.body: Use this lesson language to communicate a simple real-life meaning: Use this is, my, his, and her to identify family members. Model: “This is my brother, and his name is Bao.” Notice the important words and the word order. Mẹo tiếng Việt: hãy hiểu ý của cả câu trước, rồi nói theo cụm ngắn; không cần dịch từng từ.
content_sections.title: Form and meaning

content_sections.body: Read this short situation. A learner needs to use my family clearly and politely. One useful response is: “This is my brother, and his name is Bao.” Say the model once, then change one safe detail such as a name, place, time, colour, or item when the meaning allows.
content_sections.title: Guided context

content_sections.body: Practise for meaning, not only for memory. Imagine one everyday situation where my family is useful. First use the model, then make one small change. Check: Is the message clear? Is the target language in the right place? Can another person answer you?
content_sections.title: Use it

exercises.prompt: Read the short message and answer the question about my family.
exercises.stimulus: This is my brother, and his name is Bao.

exercises.prompt: Put these two parts in a natural order to make a message about my family.
Make a short, personal response about my family. Use the lesson language and add one detail that is yours.

criteria: The response communicates a clear meaning about my family.
The response uses the allocated language in an understandable form.
The response adds an appropriate personal or invented detail.

language_focus: Use this is, my, his, and her to identify family members.
objectives: Use this is, my, his, and her to identify family members.
Use family words in one short, clear everyday exchange.

constraints: Do not reveal the transcript before the learner answers.
Ask exactly one comprehension question before showing the transcript.
Use only the supplied project-authored transcript.
listening.goal: Understand one clear detail in a short exchange about my family.
listening.instruction: Listen once without reading to a short exchange about my family. Answer the question, then ask to see the transcript and listen again.
listening.question: What is the sister's name?
listening.transcript: This is my sister. Her name is Hoa, and she is ten.

constraints: Assess pronunciation only when learner audio is available.
Return NOT_ASSESSED when no audio is supplied.
Give one observable sound, stress, or rhythm point rather than general pronunciation advice.
pronunciation.goal: Produce the identified sound, stress, or rhythm feature clearly in a useful phrase.
pronunciation.instruction: Read the concrete sound target aloud: Say my and her clearly; do not add a vowel before the /h/ in her. Then read one lesson sentence slowly and once at normal speed.
pronunciation.target: Say my and her clearly; do not add a vowel before the /h/ in her.

constraints: Give the tutor one role and the learner one role before the first turn.
Create an information gap: the tutor asks for one missing personal or practical detail.
Use no more than three tutor turns and give one correction only if it blocks meaning.
Finish after the learner has used the target and responded to one follow-up.
speaking.goal: Complete a short, understandable exchange about my family.
speaking.instruction: Roleplay: you are a learner using my family; the tutor is a helpful conversation partner. Scenario: you need to use this language in a short everyday interaction. Tutor opening: “Hello. Can we practise my family?” Reply naturally, ask or answer one follow-up question, and finish the exchange politely. Useful model: This is my brother, and his name is Bao.

constraints: Wait for the learner draft before feedback.
Give at most two brief improvement points about meaning, word order, or target use.
Do not replace the learner draft with a complete rewritten answer.
writing.goal: Produce a short A1 message about my family with a clear meaning.
writing.instruction: Write 2–3 short sentences for a real-life situation about my family. Include one sentence pattern from this lesson, then add one true or invented detail. Do not copy this model exactly: This is my brother, and his name is Bao. Submit your draft first.
